name: above head chest stretch
interpretation: Symmetric standing demonstration begins with fingers linked in front of the body. The linked hands travel in a forward clearance arc to overhead, palms outward/up, then slightly behind the shoulder line. A small upper-thoracic lift opens the chest; pelvis and lumbar pitch remain unchanged. Fingers stay linked while the arms lower gently to release the stretch and close the loop. Relaxed shoulders and steady breathing are represented by a quiet, unbounced hold rather than an invented breathing motion. The catalogue conditional side-switch cue does not apply to this symmetric staging. The 5-second illustration compresses the source 20–30-second workout hold.

authored_choices.stance: Original bilateral standing feet, hip/knee geometry and pelvis position preserved.
authored_choices.grip: Loose articulated bilateral interlaced finger hooks; right wrist offset 14 mm along the finger row and 20 mm along palm normal keeps actual surfaces from crossing. Palms turn outward/up during the rise. Illustration spacing, not an anatomical prescription.
authored_choices.angle_status: Reversible authored world-X staging values, not validated anatomical targets.
authored_choices.support_surface: Plane Blender-world Z=0; both heel and forefoot skin patches stay grounded through all phases.
authored_choices.muscle_display: Cyan soft stretch fields for source pectorals; softer source shoulders and upper chest. Root integrates the common runtime field, no texture maps.
authored_choices.cameras: Front oblique exposes bilateral chest, hands and feet; side oblique exposes overhead/back reach, lumbar contour and hand/scalp clearance.
authored_choices.arm_orientation: Minimum-rotation upper arm; forearm frame transported from upper arm before elbow flexion to avoid the independent antiparallel shortest-arc roll.

instructions: Stand tall and interlace your fingers, then raise your arms overhead.
Press your arms slightly back and lift your chest without arching your lower back.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
